name: Chöd: the visualized offering of the body (lus sbyin)
method_summary: Summary only (restricted). After refuge, bodhicitta and supplication to Machig and the lineage, the practitioner transfers consciousness into the sky as the wrathful ḍākinī, visualizes the body left behind as offered and transformed into nectar, and distributes it to the four guests, then rests in the view in which giver, gift and recipient are empty; sung liturgy with drum, bell and thighbone trumpet. Its purpose is to cut self-clinging, not to subdue spirits.
prerequisites: Chöd empowerment and reading transmission from a lineage holder
some understanding of the view of emptiness
the teacher's permission before practice in frightening places
signs_of_progress: fear no longer arises in frightening places

warnings.text: Practised without the view of emptiness and without compassion it becomes a mere rite that can provoke harm.
Do not go to frightening places before the teacher permits and before one has stability.
Pride at feeling powerful over spirits is itself the māra of conceit.
Spirits are guests to be fed with compassion, not enemies to be attacked or exorcised.

equivalents.note: the kusāli's accumulation of the Nyingma preliminaries is a short form of the same visualized body-offering
both practise in charnel grounds to overcome fear and clinging; their views, deities and aims differ

name: Chöd practice in charnel grounds and haunted places
method_summary: Summary only (restricted). Having trained in the liturgy, the practitioner goes to charnel grounds and places held to be haunted, practises Chöd there, especially at night, and meets the fear that arises by looking for the one who is afraid; wandering practitioners traditionally moved between many such places.
prerequisites: stable practice of the Chöd liturgy

warnings.text: Not to be undertaken before the teacher permits and before one has stability; practised with self-clinging it increases fear and harm.

name: Pacification practice (zhi byed)
method_summary: Instructions of Padampa Sangye for pacifying suffering: renunciation and devotion, resting the mind in the emptiness taught by the Perfection of Wisdom, and sūtra and mantra methods arranged along the five paths (details of the individual instructions not recalled).

name: The preliminaries of the Jonang vajra-yoga
method_summary: The common and uncommon preliminaries (refuge, bodhicitta, purification, maṇḍala offering, guru yoga) done in the Kālacakra form before the six-branch yoga is taught (details not recalled).

name: Daily, seasonal and occasional conduct (spyod lam)
method_summary: Regular sleep, oil massage and moderate exercise; moral conduct and gentle speech as part of health; adjusting diet and activity to the six seasons; not suppressing the natural urges.

name: Dietary regimen by nyepa and season
method_summary: Choosing foods by taste and potency to balance rlung, mkhris pa and bad kan; eating in measure (half food, a quarter drink, a quarter empty); avoiding incompatible foods.

name: Kunye (bsku mnye) oil massage
method_summary: Massage with warmed oils, especially for rlung disorders, the elderly and in daily conduct (method details not recorded).

name: External therapies (bloodletting, moxibustion, compresses, baths)
method_summary: Summary only (restricted: includes bloodletting). 'Rough' and 'gentle' external therapies used when medicines do not suffice — bloodletting for hot and blood disorders, moxibustion for cold and rlung, hot and cold compresses, medicinal and mineral baths, minor surgery. Sites, instruments and procedures are not recorded.

warnings.text: To be applied only by trained physicians after diagnosis; the wrong therapy aggravates the disorder (the texts' general teaching).

name: Essence extraction (bcud len)
method_summary: Summary only (restricted where it restricts ordinary food). Rejuvenating regimens in which the practitioner, often in retreat, lives on or supplements food with prepared essences (of flowers, minerals and other substances) to restore vigour, prolong life and support meditation.

warnings.text: To be undertaken only with instruction from a qualified teacher and physician; unsuitable regimens harm health (tradition's general caution).

name: Medicine Buddha practice and consecration of medicines (sman sgrub)
method_summary: Visualizing the Medicine Buddha, reciting his mantra and supplication, and in the physicians' tradition consecrating medicines in a group ritual so that the mantra and the practitioners' samādhi empower them.

equivalents.note: sūtra-based Bhaiṣajyaguru rites for the sick

name: Yuthok Nyingthig: guru yoga and practice of the physicians
method_summary: The physician's spiritual path: preliminaries, guru yoga of Yuthok, generation and completion practices, so that medicine and Dharma are practised together.

equivalents.note: guru yoga with Yuthok as the guru

name: The three-year retreat in Kongtrul's system
method_summary: A closed retreat of about three years under strict rules, in which retreatants complete the preliminaries and then the practices of several lineages in sequence (among them the Shangpa instructions and the Kālacakra six-branch yoga), as set out in Kongtrul's retreat manual.
duration: about three years (three years and three fortnights)
notes: Duration formula and curriculum order recalled with low confidence.
